text:
olivia: hitting a 401 on the ruby quickstart sampleapp after switching to the refreshable token flow. no errors on token creation, just 401 from /v1/chat. Anyone seen this?
ben: hmm, is the app sending the header as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` or is it raw key?
olivia: using the example env var in README, so the sample does `headers['Authorization'] = "Bearer "+ENV['REDWOOD_API_KEY']` — here's the log: `{"error":"unauthorized","status":401}`
lee: could be a newline or extra whitespace on the env value. also check the token lifetime — are you passing a short-lived refresh token instead of the access token?
olivia: good call, i copied from the cli output which had a trailing newline. trimmed it and still 401. token is 1h access token from the refresh flow.
ben: can you dump the exact header bytes (obfuscate token) e.g. `puts headers.inspect` before request? also are you using the hosted endpoint or a private deploy?
olivia: hosted. header dump: `{\"Authorization\"=>\"Bearer sk_live_...\"}`
lee: that looks right. Do you maybe have an old gem version? `gem list redwood` shows 0.3.1? we had an auth bug fixed in 0.3.2.
olivia: whoops, i'm on 0.3.0. upgrading now.
devex-bot: quick reference: auth parity fixes for Ruby in changelog: https://redwood.example/changelog#ruby-0-3-2 :package:
ben: if upgrade doesn't fix it, try `bundle exec ruby sample.rb` after `bundle update redwood-sdk` and paste the small failing curl output.
olivia: upgraded to 0.3.2, retried, works! :tada: no 401 anymore.
olivia: filing a tiny docs PR to mention the common newline pitfall in the onboarding steps. cc @ben @lee
ben: awesome — thanks! opened #345 to add a troubleshooting note and a test that trims env vars in CI.
lee: can we also add a small note in the ruby sampleapp README about the refreshable-token helper and `strip`? saves folks 10m of debugging.
olivia: agreed, will add a one-liner and link to the refreshable token helper.
ben: nice minimal win for DX. :+1:
